a.d: Park leży 26 kilometrów na wschód od Tirany i obejmuje górę Dajti wraz z sąsiednimi szczytami. Sama góra wznosi się na 1613 metrów, a na terenie parku są kanion Brari, osmański most kamienny i jaskinie.
Meczet Ethema Beja (alb. Xhamia e Haxhi Et'hem Beut) – meczet znajdujący się w Tiranie, stolicy Albanii na Placu Skanderbega.
a.de: Construction of this mosque took about 28 years and finished in 1821. It is considered one of the most beautiful mosques in Albania with very interesting decorations and artwork within it. Reopened in 2021 after full restoration.

a.d: Plac Skanderbega – plac w centrum Tirany. Nazwa placu pochodzi od Skanderbega, albańskiego przywódcy, powstańca i bohatera narodowego.
a.de: Tirana's city centre. A statue of Albanian hero Skanderbeg stands in the square with the Albanian flag on the side. Renovations have made the square pedestrians and public transportation friendly. Government buildings featuring Italian architecture and some structures outlined below are all right of

a.d: Narodowe Muzeum Historyczne (alb. Muzeu Historik Kombëtar) – największe muzeum albańskie otwarte 28 października 1981, z siedzibą w Tiranie, mieszczące się w budynku zaprojektowanym przez grupę architektów pod kierunkiem Envera Faji.
a.de: The largest museum in Albania holds many of the country's archaeological treasures and a replica of Skanderbeg's massive sword (how he held it, rode his horse and fought at the same time, is a mystery). The lighting might be poor but the excellent collection is almost entirely signed in English and

a.de: Completely renovated and reopened in May 2023, the pyramid was built in 1987 according to the design of Enver Hoxha's daughter and was opened as a museum dedicated to her father. In 2007 US President George W. Bush gave a speech in front of this building. The building was the most expensive erected

a.d: Wieża zegarowa w Tiranie – wieża z zegarami wzniesiona w 1. połowie XIX wieku w Tiranie, zabytek I kategorii.
a.de: This tower has become a symbol of Tirana. It is one of the oldest constructions in Tirana, built in the 1820s. Don't forget to visit the nearby Clock Towers of Albania Museum featuring Clock Towers from around Albania, and traditional costumes from Tirana region. The stairs have 90 steps that go in

a.d: Muzeum Podsłuchu Służb Państwowych (alb. Muzeu i Përgjimeve të Sigurimit të Shtetit), znane również jako Dom Liści (Shtëpia me Gjethe), to muzeum historyczne w Tiranie w Albanii.
a.de: This grand old 1930s building started life as Albania's first maternity hospital, but within a few years the focus turned from creating new lives to ending lives as the hospital was converted to an interrogation and surveillance centre (read: torture house). It remained as such until the fall of the

a.d: Teatr Narodowy w Tiranie (alb. Teatri Kombëtar) – narodowa scena Albanii, znajdująca się w dawnym budynku Kinoteatru Kosowa, wzniesionego w 1939 w Tiranie.
Most Garbarzy (alb. Ura e Tabakëve) – najstarszy zachowany most w Tiranie, pochodzący z czasów osmańskich.
a.de: This is an 18th-century Ottoman period stone footbridge. The bridge was once part of the Shëngjergj Road that linked Tirana with the eastern highlands. The Shëngjergj Road furnished the city with agricultural produce and livestock. The bridge went across the Lanë stream and was adjacent to the area

a.d: Katedra Zmartwychwstania Pańskiego (alb. Katedralja Ngjallja e Krishtit) – katedra Autokefalicznego Prawosławnego Kościoła Albanii, wzniesiona na początku XXI wieku.
a.de: This cathedral features fascinating architecture and rich interior iconography. The church covered with a 23-m-high dome

a.d: Pałac Kultury w Tiranie (alb. Pallati i Kulturës) – budynek użyteczności publicznej znajdujący się w centrum Tirany, stanowiący siedzibę dla Biblioteki Narodowej Albanii oraz Teatru Opery i Baletu.
Katedra Świętego Pawła (alb. Katedralja e Shen Palit) – rzymskokatolicka katedra archidiecezji Tirany-Durrës w stolicy Albanii - Tiranie.
a.de: This modern cathedral features fascinating window murals.

a.d: Muzeum Archeologiczne w Tiranie (alb. Muzeu Arkeologjik i Tiranës) – muzeum archeologiczne działające w Tiranie, powołane do życia 1 listopada 1948 roku.
a.de: Features ancient artifacts from Illyrian to Roman and Hellenic times: wonderful mosaics, Roman statues and illustrative maps. The collection here is comprehensive and impressive in parts, but there's only minimal labelling in Albanian and none at all in English (nor are tours in English offered), so

a.d: Narodowa Galeria Sztuki w Tiranie (alb. Galeria Kombëtare e Arteve) – państwowa galeria sztuki w Tiranie, założona w 1954.
a.de: Tracing the relatively brief history of Albanian painting from the early 19th century to the present day, this beautiful space also has temporary exhibitions. The interesting collection includes 19th-century paintings depicting scenes from daily Albanian life and others with a far more political dim

a.d: Zamek w Petreli (alb. Kalaja e Petrelës) – zamek we wsi Petrelë, w środkowej Albanii, ok.
a.de: This is one of Albania's best-preserved castles. It is known as an ancient settlement 2000 years old and was commanded by princess Mamica, the sister of the national hero, Skanderbeg.

a.d: Grobowiec Kaplana Paszy – kamienny grobowiec (türbe) z 1. połowy XIX wieku w Tiranie, zabytek I kategorii.
a.de: Built in 1820, originally next to a mosque which was destroyed during WWII. Kapllan Pasha was an Ottoman ruler of Tirana who was buried here, but his remains were later moved to Istanbul.

a.d: Drugi co do wielkości plac Tirany, zaplanowany przez włoskiego architekta Gherardo Bosio i zbudowany w latach 1939–1941. Przy placu stoją między innymi Uniwersytet Tirański i Politechnika.

a.de: The history of this castle in dates back before 1300 and is a remnant from the Byzantine-era. The fortress is the place where the main east-west and north-south roads crossed, and formed the heart of Tirana. About all that's left of the fortress above ground is a 6-m-high Ottoman-era wall, covered i

a.n: Zemra e Krishtit Catholic Church of Tirana
Mausoleum of the Albanian Royal Family

a.d: Centralny park publiczny Tirany, założony w 1950 roku w epoce komunistycznej. Na północy sąsiaduje z Teatrem Lalek i soborem prawosławnym, a od wschodu z bulwarem Męczenników Narodu.
Hotel Dajti – dawny hotel w Tiranie znajdujący się w centrum miasta, przy bulwarze Dëshmorët e Kombit.
Chanaka Sheh Dyrri w Tiranie (alb. Teqeja e Sheh Dyrrit) – chanaka znajdująca się w Tiranie, w Albanii.
a.de: This is a teqe (teqe or cemevi is a Turkish meeting house for communal worship service) in Tirana. Back in the day it was also the home of a local sheikh. It's listed as a cultural monument of Albania, however it's private property and can likely only be seen from the outside.

a.d: Postbllok (alb. Memoriali Postbllok) – instalacja przestrzenna projektu Fatosa Lubonji i Ardiana Isufiego w Tiranie, upamiętniająca ofiary czasów komunizmu.
Matka Albania (alb. Nëna Shqipëri) – 12-metrowy pomnik znajdujący się na Cmentarzu Narodowych Męczenników Albanii (alb.
Osmański meczet z 1750 roku, jeden z niewielu, które przetrwały rządy komunistów. W 1966 roku zamieniono go w magazyn żywności, a w 1991 roku przywrócono go wiernym.
a.de: Finished in 1750 during Ottoman rule and one of the few that survived the Communist rule intact. During that time the building functioned as a storehouse and a tobacco shop, then in 1991 it was returned to its original use.

a.d: Meczet stoi przy Moście Garbarzy, w dawnej dzielnicy cechu garbarzy z czasów osmańskich. W latach 1967–1990 był zamknięty, a po ponownym otwarciu opiekuje się nim rodzina Resmja.
a.de: Built in the 17th century in a part of the city where leather workers lived. It was largely destroyed by a lightning strike in 1927, but quickly rebuilt. This museum features the fauna and geological composition of Albania.

The mosaic was discovered following excavations for an apartment complex. Various artifacts point to the presence of a village in the area thousands of years ago. This is the only archaeological site in Tirana.

The little cousin to the main Bunk'art, this museum, which is within a communist-era bunker and underground tunnel system below the ministry of Interior Affairs, focuses on the role of the police and security services in Albania through the turbulent 20th century. As non-profit exhibition space founded in 2007. With its 150 m² area on the second floor of a mixed residential and commercial building at Abdyl Frashëri Street No.7 in the Blloku area of Tirana (zona Libri Universitar: between Santa Margherita Wine Shop and LC Waikiki Store), ZETA functions as an a

a.n: The Museum of the Bank of Albania
a.d: Bank Albanii (alb. Banka e Shqipërisë) – albański bank centralny z siedzibą w Tiranie.
a.de: The museum lies on two floors, each of which is conceived as an independent space from the other. On the first floor is presented the rich numismatic collection of the Bank of Albania from antiquity to the present day. The second floor of the museum presents the history of the central bank instituti

The museum presents, through documents, photos and original objects, the history of Bektashism (an Islamic Sufistic movement) on a world scale and in particular of Albanian Bektashism. It is organized in 12 stands of 12 showcases, observing the 12 Imams. A very important angle is the one devoted to

a.n: Historical Museum of the Armed Forces
a.de: This museum contains more than a thousand objects, from the Middle Ages to the 19th century, decorated with gold and silver, a range of display cases with rifles of various types of Medieval, Renaissance, Skanderbeg's swords, of Ali Pasha Tepelena, aircraft, helicopters, tanks, four silhouettes, gro

This apartment was the residence of Kadare, an important writer, from 1974 to 1989, and his work place. It was designed by architect Maks Velo in 1972, was declared category II Culture Monument in 2015. The modernist and cubist building was called at that time "the palace with cubes", and represents
This street was named after US President George W. Bush in honour of his 2007 visit.

Among the apartment blocks, one can find some of Tirana's trendiest cafés, shops, and restaurants. Here is also located the villa of the former dictator, Enver Hoxha. During communism, the area was reserved solely for government officials and was not allowed to be entered by the commoner. It was ope

a.d: Biblioteka Narodowa Albanii (alb. Biblioteka Kombëtare e Shqipërisë, BKSh) – albańska biblioteka narodowa, znajdująca się w Tiranie.
a.de: The library holds over a million books and is known for its ancient collections.
This well-preserved traditional house owned by painter Sali Shijaku features art displays, traditional house emnities, and a restaurant.

This is the cemetery where the remains of 900 partisans that fought for Tirana are buried. Here one can also find the 12-m statue of Mother Albania built in 1972 (Monumenti Nëna Shqipëri). Hoxha was buried here in 1985 but exhumed in 1992 and moved to the other side of the city.
This 15th-century castle is on the picturesque hills of Preze village west of Rinas airport.
An archaeological site comprising the remains of a Roman fortification (built over an earlier Illyrian castle) on a mountainside of Mount Dajti.
Located on a pyramid-shaped hill. A cobblestone paved pass lead to the castle.

Persqopi was an ancient city. It's on the Viles Hillside (malin e Vilës). The outer wall was 7 m high, the bastion 12 m high. The city is built using more than 2 m long and 1 m high stone elements. Take a stroll around the hill.
Murat Toptani Street is a pedestrian-only street east of Rinia Park constructed with stone near the Tirana Castle walls. Traditional houses, cafes, and a local park are found here.

a.n: Stroll along Bulevardi Dëshmorët e Kombit
a.de: A panoramic boulevard built by the Italians in the 1930s similar to the Champs de Elysee extending south from Skanderberg Square. The boulevard features Fascist, Communist, and modern architecture of government buildings, business centres and hotels. Many local parks are found here. This street runs

This beautiful place in the heart of downtown Tirana. It includes restaurants, casinos, bars, a club, etc. It is surrounded by a huge lit water fountain with a glowing bridge that reaches to the restaurant, and is an ideal place for all ages. Children enjoy gourmet ice cream and iced European soft d

a.n: Grand Park along the Artificial Lake
a.de: People have picnics and have fun, and the natural beauty allows it because of the huge trees, open spaces, and mountains surrounding them. An artificial lake lies in the middle of the Park. It is popular with locals and tourists as a place to walk around and enjoy a lunch or coffee at one of the res

The Ali-Demi skate park is a great place to go with your family because there is a nice park on one of the sides next to the skate park, there are markets, and a beautiful café shop with a playground for small children with typical swings and benches and soccer fields in the back. The skate park is

a.n: Mount Dajti National Park & Cable Car
a.d: Park Narodowy Dajti ((alb.) Parku Kombëtar Dajti) obejmuje obszar 29 216,9 hektarów w okręgu Tirana w Albanii. Znajduje się 26 kilometrów na wschód od Tirany.
a.de: The most accessible mountain in the country, and many locals go there to escape the city rush and have a spit-roast lamb lunch. A sky-high, Austrian-made cable car, Dajti Express, takes 15 minutes to make the scenic trip (almost) to the top (1,611 m). Visit the new Visitor's Centre near the radio&TV
A panoramic canyon and Ottoman bridge just steps from the capital. Spectacular views of the surrounding mountains and Tirana. A cave and a beautiful waterfall is found near Shengjergj village.

There are many small resorts and restaurants in Tirana's greenbelt areas of Berzhite, Petrela, and Farke along Rruga e Elbasanit and SH3. One locality features shooting range facilities, a modest golf club and horse riding, while others traditional food, wooden villa accommodations, and swimming poo

A fun mini-golf course, the only 18-hole course in the country. Suitable for players of all ages and with no previous experience needed. With a number of obstacles in your way, the aim of the game is to get your ball into the hole in the least amount of shots. The course is equipped with floodlighti
Popular weekend beach retreat where small seaside resorts can be found. This is also where Albania's wealthy rest. Visit Skanderbeg Castle along the cost, and a small church at Rodon Cape nearby.

A popular seaside weekend retreat. The name stems from an Italian general who used to rest at this beach during World War II. Accommodation is available in form of wooden villas. An international resort is also being build nearby at Kalaja e Turres. Visit nearby Bashtova Castle and Shenepremte Churc

a.d: Meczet stoi na Placu Skanderbega, a jego budowę rozpoczęto w 1789 roku i ukończono w 1823 roku. Za Envera Hodży był jedynym czynnym meczetem w kraju, a wnętrze zdobią freski i sztukaterie.
Meczet wzniesiony w latach 2015–2022 w centrum stolicy Albanii. Jest największym meczetem na Bałkanach, a jego budowę finansował głównie rząd Turcji.
Muzeum poświęcone Skanderbegowi, otwarte 1 listopada 1982 roku w Krui. Mieści się w głębi zamku, obok Muzeum Etnograficznego, a sam zamek jest symbolem oporu Albańczyków.
Najstarszy zachowany most w Tiranie, kamienny, trzyprzęsłowy, pochodzący z czasów osmańskich. Wzniesiono go pod koniec XVIII wieku nad rzeką Laną, a łączy centrum miasta z jego częścią wschodnią.
Zbiornik zaporowy na północny wschód od Tirany, w granicach Parku Narodowego Dajti. Dostarcza większość wody pitnej dla stolicy, a zapora ma 91 metrów wysokości.
Meczet w historycznym bazarze Krui, ukończony w 1533 roku, jest zabytkiem kultury Albanii. W czasach dyktatury zamknięto go i zburzono minaret, a w 1991 roku przywrócono go wiernym.
Park o powierzchni 289 hektarów w południowej części miasta, z sztucznym jeziorem. Na jego terenie stoją kościół Świętego Prokopa i Pałac Prezydencki oraz pomniki albańskich postaci.
Ogród założony na 15 hektarach w południowej części miasta i udostępniony zwiedzającym w 1971 roku. Rośnie w nim około 3250 gatunków roślin, w tym 2000 rodzimych.
Międzynarodowe centrum zakonu bektaszytów, sufickiego bractwa, na wschodnim skraju Tirany. Znajdują się tam także muzeum, biblioteka i archiwum.
Mauzoleum, w którym spoczywa król Zog I wraz z członkami rodziny. Pierwotny budynek z 1935 roku zniszczyli komuniści w 1944 roku, a replikę odsłonięto w 2012 roku.
Chanaka z drugiej połowy XVIII wieku w północnej części Tirany, należąca do bractwa Kadirije. W 1967 roku częściowo ją zniszczono w okresie ateizacji kraju, a w 1990 roku odbudowano.
Krasowa jaskinia w wąwozie Skorana koło wsi Pëllumbas, w granicach Parku Narodowego Dajti. Uważana jest za jedną z najpiękniejszych jaskiń w kraju i ma ślady kultury z epoki paleolitu.

Stanowisko archeologiczne z mozaikami z rzymskiego domu z III wieku i bazyliką paleochrześcijańską z V i VI wieku. To jedyny zabytek archeologiczny w granicach miasta, a mozaiki przedstawiają drób i ryby.
Stanowisko archeologiczne na wzgórzu na zachodnim zboczu Dajti, z ruinami rzymskiej fortyfikacji i kilku domostw. Odkryto je w 1963 roku, a wzniesiono prawdopodobnie na iliryjskich fundamentach.
